newsitem.title: EAST TIMOR: New Catholic bishop installed in East Timor.
newsitem.headline: New Catholic bishop installed in East Timor.

text.p: A Portuguese archbishop on Wednesday installed a new Catholic bishop in East Timor, underlining church efforts to bring peace to the troubled territory annexed by Indonesia more than two decades ago.
Maurilio Gouveia, archbishop of Evera in Portugal, installed Basilio Do Nascimento as bishop of the newly created diocese of Baucau covering the eastern end of East Timor.
Gouveia stood in for the papal nuncio (ambassador) to Jakarta, Monseigneur Pietro Sambi, who was taken ill on Tuesday night and had to return to the territory's capital of Dili.
About 20,000 people gathered in steamy tropical sunshine in the Baucau town square for the Mass following Nascimento's installation.
The crowd was quiet and orderly and there were no reports of trouble.

Pope John Paul split East Timor into two diocese late last year to improve church administration and help ease the burden on the territory's other bishop, the popular Carlos Belo, who shared the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to bring peace and reconciliation to East Timor.

Indonesia invaded the territory, about 2,000 km (1,250 miles) east of Jakarta, in December 1975 as civil war raged after the withdrawal of the Portuguese colonial rulers. It incorporated East Timor as Indonesia's 27th province the next July in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
